scope.purpose: Assess a fast3-family speed-side alternative under the current same-hotkey payout constraint; the main round10 objective remains balanced-frontier research.

payability_context.condition_for_a_new_point_to_replace_453: The new point must dominate #453 in official score geometry and remain eligible; admission, registration ownership, bounty eligibility, and any resulting award remain UNKNOWN and unauthorized for action.

candidate.name: r3-432-fast3
candidate.proof_relation: Parse.lean is byte-identical to the #432 proof per candidate manifest; round03 records successful fresh official extraction and gate for the derivative.
candidate.attribution: Public #432 derivative, not an independent algorithm.

measurement_source.per_block: 28 files, one warmup and 11 measured repetitions per method and file.

observed_public_metrics.interpretation: Time axis is the equal-file mean, for each block, of median measured total_s(candidate)/median measured total_s(incumbent); block results are then equally weighted. Size is equal-file output_bytes/raw_bytes.

component_share_model.method: For every file in every block, take the median of the 11 measured parser time_s values and the median of the 11 measured encode_s values; calculate each component's share of their sum, then average the 112 file-block shares equally.
component_share_model.caveat: Component shares are diagnostic medians, not the official score metric; the median of per-repetition total_s need not equal the sum of component medians.

free_parser_sensitivity.assumption: Set parser time to zero while leaving each observed fast3 encoder time unchanged; use the observed incumbent median total_s as denominator for each file and block, then average equally across 112 observations.
free_parser_sensitivity.status: Sensitivity ceiling only; not a measured or attainable speedup and not a confidence bound.

failed_or_exhausted_directions.evidence: Round03 records fast2 as slower and larger than fast3; it was rejected.

failed_or_exhausted_directions.direction: NICE and nearby skip/depth parameter search
failed_or_exhausted_directions.evidence: Optimization methods records nice16/nice64 without stable time benefit. Round03 dmin257 and tshift3 had narrow calibrated geometry but missed the fixed #427 screening threshold.

Closing read-ahead was about 1.78% slower and forced non-inline run1 about 4.32% slower. run1tai's roughly 0.277% gain across one runner's blocks reversed to a loss on an independent runner; foldni's small initial gain washed out. Five further CPU rewrites were initially 0.55%-1.14% slower, and the independent CPU variants did not establish a repeatable total-time gain.
Round04 reports lazy4far about 0.179% slower with 36.577230% size; lazy9-cost and classoutline were slower on the independent runner. Short remote-cost rejection variants had no useful two-axis gain.

probe_recommendation.reason: No distinct, low-proof-cost fast3 probe is supported by current evidence as likely to improve total time while holding output size equal or smaller. Parser is only about 16.4% of measured parser-plus-encoder component time, the official encoder dominates, and prior output-preserving CPU rewrites were slower or failed independent replication. Search-budget changes already show the speed/size tradeoff and provide no small-output-preserving path.

VERIFIED: Raw measurement hashes, source/proof hashes, four-block metrics, and per-file component calculations in this audit.
Round03/round04 documented gate and performance outcomes for the named variants.
INFERRED: The free-parser floor and its score-axis reduction are a counterfactual model.
No probe is recommended based on the limited prior CPU and parameter-search evidence.
UNKNOWN: Whether any untested parser change could preserve all outputs and produce a reproducible improvement large enough to dominate #453.
